deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page sets up a Helmholtz/Klein-Gordon-type equation u_xx + u_yy = mu^2 u. It transports this equation through the conformal map x+iy = ∫ dz/sqrt(z(z-e^{iψ})(z-e^{-iψ})) and expands (1 - e^{i(φ+ψ)} r)^(-1/2) in powers. The next page treats eigenfunctions of the form cos(sqrt(1-λ)x) and cos(sqrt(-1-λ)x). There u is split as u1 = (u - Δu)/2 and u2 = (u + Δu)/2, with Δu1 + u1 = 0 and Δu2 - u2 = 0. This split is exactly what one does for Δ²u = u, the vibrating-plate (Chladni) equation, with boundary data on x = ±a. This page is a power-series computation for that cluster of problems. Its exact governing equation is not written on the page, so the reading below is partly conjectural, as marked.

(1) Ansatz. Riemann writes Π(k) = k! (Gauss notation). In two real variables p, q the ansatz is
u = Σ_{m,n} a_m p^{m+2n} q^{2n} / (Π(m+2n) Π(2n)) + Σ_{m,n} b_m p^{m+2n-1} q^{2n+1} / (Π(m+2n-1) Π(2n+1)).
Define the basis functions A_m = Σ_n p^{m+2n} q^{2n}/((m+2n)!(2n)!) and B_m = Σ_n p^{m+2n-1} q^{2n+1}/((m+2n-1)!(2n+1)!). Then u = Σ a_m A_m + Σ b_m B_m. A_m is even in q and B_m is odd in q.

(2) Shift rules (filled in by me; they follow from differentiating term by term).
- ∂_p² A_m = A_{m-2} and ∂_q² A_m = A_{m+2}.
- Likewise ∂_p² B_m = B_{m-2} and ∂_q² B_m = B_{m+2}.
- First derivatives map between the families, e.g. ∂_q B_m = A_{m-1} and ∂_p A_m = A_{m-1}.
Hence (∂_p² + ∂_q²) Σ a_m A_m = Σ (a_{m+2} + a_{m-2}) A_m. That is the line 'Σ(a_{m+2}+a_{m-2}) p^{m+2n}/Π(m+2n) · q^{2n}/Π2n'. The b-part gives b_{m+2} + b_{m-2}; on the page it appears as b_{m+3} + b_{m-1} under a shifted labelling.

(3) Boundary line. The line '∂u/∂x, x=0 | Σ a_m p^{m+2n-2}/Π(m+2n-2) …, b_{m+1}' differentiates the ansatz and evaluates it on a boundary line. A first-order derivative takes B to A with an index shift, hence the b_{m+1}.

(4) Mixed coefficients. Riemann then collects coefficient combinations that mix the two families:
- a_{m+2} + a_{m-2} + (4r-2) b_{m+2}, and b_{m+2} + b_{m-2} + (4r-2) a_{m-2};
- a_{m+3} - (4r+1) a_{m-1} - (4r+1) b_{m+3} + b_{m-1}, and b_{m+3} - (4r+1) b_{m-1} - (4r+1) a_{m-1} + a_{m-5}.
The parameter r is not defined on the page; it is presumably a constant of the problem or an index.

(5) Second set. He rewrites both lines with the sign of every cross term between the a- and b-families reversed. The higher-order line is multiplied by i. This is consistent with replacing q by -q (B is odd in q) or with a conjugate / rotated combination, i.e. taking real and imaginary parts.

(6) Restriction to the diagonal p = q = x. Both a-type terms p^{m+2n} q^{2n} and b-type terms p^{m+2n-1} q^{2n+1} become x^{m+4n}. The result is
Σ (a_{m+2} + a_{m-2} - (4r-2) b_{m+2}) x^{m+4n}/(Π(m+2n) Π2n) + Σ (b_{m+2} + b_{m-2} - (4r-2) a_{m-2}) x^{m+4n}/(Π(m+2n-1) Π(2n+1)).

(7) Coefficient condition. Put μ = m + 4n, so m+2n = μ-2n. Requiring each power x^μ to vanish gives
Σ_n [ (a_{μ+2-4n} + a_{μ-2-4n} - (4r-2) b_{μ+2-4n}) / (Π(μ-2n) Π(2n)) + (b_{μ+2-4n} + b_{μ-2-4n} - (4r-2) a_{μ-2-4n}) / (Π(μ-2n-1) Π(2n+1)) ] = 0.
This is a linear recurrence/constraint on the coefficients, imposing a boundary condition along the diagonal line.

Purpose (conjectural). The page builds general series solutions and turns a boundary condition into linear equations for the coefficients. This fits the boundary-value/eigenvalue problem of the neighbouring pages (Helmholtz equation, or the plate equation Δ²u = u), likely for a domain bounded by straight lines at 45° in the (p,q) variables.
errors: The b-family shift is written b_{m+3}+b_{m-1} in the upper block but b_{m+2}+b_{m-2} in the later lines. This is an inconsistent index labelling (a relabelling m -> m±1), not necessarily an error.

Several struck-out factors (e.g. '(m+2)' in front of a_{m+2} and '(m-2)' in front of b_{m+2}) show that Riemann first tried coefficient factors and then discarded them. With factorial-normalised monomials no such factors arise, so the corrections are right.
The origin of the constants (4r-2) and (4r+1) cannot be checked, because the governing equation is not written on the page.
The final-line index bookkeeping (m = μ-4n, Π(m+2n) = Π(μ-2n), Π(m+2n-1) = Π(μ-2n-1)) is correct.

results.what: Factorially normalised double power-series basis in which ∂_p² and ∂_q² act as index shifts, turning a PDE into a linear recurrence for coefficients.
results.modern_name: Power-series (Frobenius/Cauchy–Kovalevskaya-type) method for linear PDE; shift-operator recurrence
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler, Cauchy); standard by the 19th century

results.what: Restriction of the series to the diagonal p=q=x, collecting powers x^μ to impose a boundary condition.
results.modern_name: Coefficient matching for boundary conditions (series collocation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine coefficient bookkeeping for a series solution of a linear PDE, tied to Riemann's known 1850s work on boundary-value and vibration problems. There is no new result; the governing equation is not even stated.

checkable.sympy: p,q=symbols('p q'); m=5; A=lambda k: sum(p**(k+2*n)*q**(2*n)/(factorial(k+2*n)*factorial(2*n)) for n in range(0,8)); simplify(diff(A(m),p,2)-A(m-2))
checkable.asserts: ∂_p² A_m = A_{m-2}, up to truncation of the series.

checkable.sympy: simplify(diff(A(m),q,2)-A(m+2)) (compare series terms up to truncation order)
checkable.asserts: ∂_q² A_m = A_{m+2}, so Δ Σ a_m A_m has coefficient a_{m+2}+a_{m-2}.

checkable.sympy: B=lambda k: sum(p**(k+2*n-1)*q**(2*n+1)/(factorial(k+2*n-1)*factorial(2*n+1)) for n in range(0,8)); diff(B(m),p,2)-B(m-2); diff(B(m),q,2)-B(m+2)
checkable.asserts: The same shift rules hold for the odd-in-q family B_m.
On the diagonal p=q=x the monomials become x^{m+4n} with denominators Π(μ-2n)Π(2n), μ=m+4n.
